tasks.title: A question round belongs to its gate and story
tasks.objective: A pass stops treating its own recorded rounds as spent, so re-recording the same gate for the same story and task reuses them and needs no invented question, while every other pass still spends them so a round never crosses to a different gate, story or task. That is the whole change: one condition in the consumption walk. Provenance is read from where evidence already lives, so no round, schema, hook or global-gate behaviour changes. Implements decision 0067.
acceptance_criteria: Re-recording the same gate for the same story and task consumes its own existing round and requires no new question, including when the submitted round set differs from the one already stored
A round already consumed by a pass at a different gate is refused
A round already consumed by a pass for a different story is refused
A round already consumed by a pass for a different task id is refused
A gate that is not story-scoped is unchanged: it still reads the active story's rounds as well as the global ones
A story-scoped gate still consumes rounds asked before any story existed
The floor of at least one real round per gate still holds, asserted both ways
No round record, schema or hook changes, asserted by the existing ledger round shape test still passing untouched

review_budget.reason: One condition in the recorder's consumption walk and one new suite. Two earlier drafts were cut by evidence: the baseline comparator (the 93-red premise was an artefact) and the global-gate narrowing (0051's hole does not exist, and narrowing broke spec/signoff/epics, which two gate tests caught).

reviewer_focus: That the context outlives the cold reader and is cleared only when the gate pass records, since the human question comes after the reader exits
That writer and reader resolve the same directory under a ceremony target, which silently misrouted rounds before
That a task grill's rounds carry its declared task id, and empty means only a gate with no task
That legacy and scoped rounds of identical text cannot consume one another in any scan order
That the baseline comparator fails on a NEW failure rather than merely counting

tasks.title: Both grill guards read the ledger the same way
tasks.objective: Every launch appends starting, running, then a terminal row, and neither grill guard collapses them — so filtering rows by status cannot exclude a failed launch, whose starting and running rows still carry its id. The cap counts every launch regardless, and the repeat-read guard's existing failed-filter does not work. Both adopt one view that collapses rows by launch_id to the latest, so a launch whose latest row is failed spends no allowance and blocks no further read. No new ledger field.
acceptance_criteria: Rows are collapsed by launch_id to the latest row, and both guards consume that same view
A launch whose lifecycle ends starting, running, failed does not count toward the cap
That same failed launch does not make the repeat-read guard refuse, which it does today
A launch whose lifecycle ends starting, running, succeeded still counts, so the budget is not disabled
A launch whose latest row is starting or running counts as a read in flight
No new field is written to the delegation ledger, and launch_status keeps its existing values

review_budget.reason: One collapsed terminal-launch view in grill.py consumed by both guards, and one new suite seeding real row lifecycles. Two earlier drafts were cut by their own cold reads: the outcome field (the companion emits JSON, D-0032) and the escalation grant (scoping does not exist, split to T5).

reviewer_focus: That rows are collapsed by launch_id to the LATEST row, since a failed launch's starting and running rows are not failed and defeated the previous row-level filter
That the repeat-read guard's existing filter is actually fixed, not merely copied: it looks correct today and is not
That tests seed real lifecycles — starting, running, failed and starting, running, succeeded, plus standalone starting and running — rather than synthetic single rows
That a successful launch still spends an allowance, or the budget is disabled rather than corrected
That nothing new is written to the ledger, since the fix is to READ what was always there
That no answered/interrupted outcome sneaks in: deferred as D-0032 because the companion is invoked with --json

tasks.title: One producer says what a gate read, and one predicate says if it is stale
tasks.objective: A single authoritative per-gate producer returns normalised repo-relative manifest inputs, including the composite signoff gate, replacing the display text locators return today. grill.json gains an optional input_manifest that the recorder requires for new passes and validates against the tree. One freshness predicate answers every consumer. A newly accepted decision is detected by comparing accepted id sets. The pre-stage task guard is untouched.
acceptance_criteria: One per-gate producer returns normalised repo-relative input paths for all six gates, including the composite signoff gate
The recorder requires a manifest for new passes, refuses one omitting the gate artifact, and refuses digests that disagree with the tree
A pass recorded without a manifest keeps tree-based freshness, asserted against a legacy fixture, and no manifest is ever backfilled
Editing a product file absent from the manifest leaves the pass valid; editing anything present stales it
A decision newly accepted or newly superseded after recording stales the pass, detected by accepted id set comparison
One predicate answers freshness for every consumer, and the pre-stage task grill still stales on an unrelated product file

tasks.title: Post-stage task freshness keeps its selective binding
tasks.objective: Post-stage task freshness uses a canonical selective snapshot rather than a path manifest, so it stales on a changed objective, criteria or plan contract without staling on write_scope, required_tests or verify_commands. The stamp path binds delta_id only, restoring what decision 0066 already requires, so a contract re-record that leaves the delta unchanged never invalidates a clean review.
acceptance_criteria: Post-stage task freshness uses a selective snapshot preserving decision 0066's binding, not a file-only manifest
A changed objective, acceptance criterion or plan contract stales the task pass
A changed write_scope, required_tests or verify_commands does not stale it
A stage review stamp survives a contract re-record that leaves the reviewed delta unchanged
A stamp does not survive a change to the reviewed delta itself

tasks.title: An escalation grants exactly one further read, for that gate and task
tasks.objective: Recording an escalation grants exactly one further cold read scoped to the gate and task it was raised for, and that grant passes BOTH the cap and the repeat-read guard. Today an open escalation clears the cap alone, so the human is told grilling continues and is then refused by a second guard. The grant is claimed atomically and spent when the granted read completes, per the confirmed spec.
acceptance_criteria: An escalation record carries the gate and task it was raised for
An open escalation grants one further read for that gate and task, and not for any other
The granted read passes both the cap and the repeat-read guard
The grant is claimed atomically, so two concurrent launches cannot both spend it
The grant is spent when the granted read completes, per the confirmed spec
A second read without a new escalation is refused
